title: WasteTrack: receiver-side digital waste tracking records

problem_severity_frequency.rationale: Mandatory per-load digital records and two-working-day submission from 1 October 2026, evidenced by SI 2026/729 and GOV.UK service guidance.

buyer_budget_clarity.rationale: Operators of ~12,000 permitted facilities are a clear buyer with a mandated £26/year statutory fee, but a new entrant's budget is unproven.

evidence_strength.rationale: Primary legislation plus GOV.UK service design and an official approved-provider list; crowding counts come from credible secondary comparisons.

distribution.rationale: Capped at 2: trade-body and search routes are plausible but no prospects were tested, and incumbents are embedded.

differentiation.rationale: Capped at 2: 54-79 approved providers including free tiers, with tracking bundled into weighbridge and waste-management systems.

validation_speed_cost.rationale: A receiver-demand test would be cheap and fast, but the wedge evidence makes it unnecessary.

feasibility.rationale: Integration with the report-receipt-of-waste API and approval testing is achievable but adds compliance overhead.

economics.rationale: Capped at 2: untested price hypothesis (£15-£40/month/site) against free tiers and a £26/year statutory fee; margins unproven.

founder_fit.rationale: No evidence about the founder's reach into waste-management operations.

risk.rationale: No regulated activity, but regulatory timing and API dependency risk; the decisive risk is competitive, not legal.

economic_buyer.note: Operators of ~12,000 permitted waste facilities in England; the £26/year statutory operator fee is already mandated.

painful_frequent_or_budgeted.note: Per-load digital records must be submitted within two working days from 1 October 2026, with correction duties.

non_paid_distribution.note: Trade-body and search routes are plausible, but no prospects were identified against embedded incumbents.
non_paid_distribution.resolve_via: Test whether permitted-site operators would find and buy a new entrant through CIWM/trade media without paid acquisition; moot given the wedge fail.

defensible_wedge.note: 54-79 approved providers (two independent comparisons), at least two free tiers, tracking bundled into weighbridge/waste-management systems, and a free government spreadsheet fallback expected until at least October 2027.

no_network_effects_needed.note: Single-site record-keeping tool; no multi-sided network required.

plausible_margins.note: Modelled £15-£40/month/site against free incumbents and a £26/year statutory fee; unproven.
plausible_margins.resolve_via: Only relevant if a wedge existed; measure paid conversion and support cost against a free incumbent.

acceptable_risk.note: No regulated activity beyond using an approved government API; no licence to operate required.

cheap_disconfirming_test.note: A receiver-demand test is cheap, though the wedge evidence killed the idea before it ran.

not_all_optimistic.note: Would require winning share against free/embedded incumbents and timing the October 2027 carrier phase.
not_all_optimistic.resolve_via: Only relevant if a wedge existed; the incumbent evidence makes the optimistic case implausible.
